c.tagline: Live-music capital of the world, where tacos, tech, and Texas swagger collide.

taxi.fareNote: Metered city cabs exist but most people use Uber or Lyft, which are widely available across the city and at the airport.

emergency.note: 911 is the single emergency number for police, fire, and ambulance across the United States.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

hood_landmark.Zilker / Barton Hills: Barton Springs Pool Zilker Park Austin

avoid.reason: 6th St nightlife petty crime; caution in some east/southeast areas

hood_desc: The walkable core along Congress Avenue and 6th Street, packed with live-music clubs, rooftop bars, the State Capitol, and Lady Bird Lake at its feet; best for first-timers who want everything within reach.
A funky, walkable stretch of vintage shops, food trailers, boutiques, and the famous 'I love you so much' mural; the go-to for shopping, people-watching, and Instagram-ready Austin weirdness.
The city's creative, fast-gentrifying east side, full of muralled warehouses, craft breweries, taco joints, and indie art spaces; suits younger travelers chasing Austin's hip, bohemian side.
A row of converted bungalow bars and cocktail patios steps from downtown, buzzing until late; the epicenter of Austin's after-dark nightlife and food-truck scene.
A leafy, laid-back area wrapped around Zilker Park and the spring-fed Barton Springs Pool; green, family-friendly, and close to hiking trails, ideal for a calmer, outdoorsy base.

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink citywide.

transit.pay: Tap the CapMetro app, a contactless card, or buy a paper ticket. A local single bus ride is $1.25 and a day pass is $2.50; a MetroRail single ride is $3.50 and a rail day pass is $7. Kids under 6 ride free.
transit.hours: Most bus routes run roughly 5am to midnight, with several high-frequency and 24-hour routes; the MetroRail Red Line runs limited weekday commuter service plus later evening and weekend trains.

transit.m: CapMetro Route 20 bus to downtown (~30 min)

tip.r: ~18-20% is customary at restaurants and bars; $1-2 per drink at a bar and a few dollars for taxis and rideshares.

landmarks: Texas State Capitol
A grand pink-granite capitol building, taller than the U.S. Capitol, symbolizing Texas pride in downtown Austin.
Congress Avenue Bridge (Bat Bridge)
Home to the world's largest urban bat colony, drawing crowds each summer evening to watch millions take flight.
Lady Bird Lake
A scenic downtown reservoir on the Colorado River lined with hike-and-bike trails, kayakers, and skyline views.
Lady Bird Johnson Wildflower Center
A botanical garden dedicated to native Texas plants, bursting with color especially during bluebonnet season.
The University of Texas Tower
The iconic landmark clock tower of UT Austin's campus, lit orange after Longhorn victories.
Mount Bonnell
Austin's highest point, offering sweeping panoramic views of the Colorado River and city skyline, especially at sunset.
Barton Springs Pool
A spring-fed natural swimming pool in Zilker Park, kept a cool 68 degrees year-round and beloved by locals.
South Congress Avenue (SoCo)
A vibrant, quirky strip of shops, food trucks, and murals including the famous 'I Love You So Much' sign.
Austin Skyline from Zilker Park
A postcard view of downtown Austin's modern skyline rising beyond the green expanse of Zilker Park.
Pennybacker Bridge (360 Bridge)
A striking arched bridge over Lake Austin, one of the most photographed engineering landmarks in the city.

train.note: Amtrak's daily Texas Eagle is the only intercity train, running Chicago - St Louis - Dallas - Austin - San Antonio, with a through sleeper and coach continuing to Los Angeles on the Sunset Limited three days a week (Tuesdays, Thursdays and Sundays). It calls at the small station just west of downtown on North Lamar Boulevard. CapMetro's commuter Red Line runs from downtown Austin out to Leander on weekdays, but it is local transit rather than a way of leaving town. There are no international trains in Texas - rail to Mexico is freight only.

intl.to: Monterrey, San Luis Potosi, Guadalajara & central Mexico

bus.note: Tornado Bus Company operates from its own Austin terminal with through coaches into Mexico; expect a long ride and a passport check at the border, plus a Mexican FMM tourist card. Greyhound (https://www.greyhound.com/), FlixBus (https://www.flixbus.com/) and Megabus (https://us.megabus.com/) cover the domestic Texas triangle - roughly 1.5 hours to San Antonio, 3-4 hours to Dallas and 3 hours to Houston - and most pick up curbside near downtown or the university rather than at a full terminal. Book online; walk-up fares are noticeably higher.

ferry.note: Austin is well over 150 miles from the Gulf and has no ferry services; the only boats are sightseeing, kayak and party cruises on Lady Bird Lake and Lake Travis. The nearest real ferry is the free state-run Galveston to Port Bolivar crossing, about four hours away by road.
